_comment: I0 provider playbook (schema: app/domain/playbook.py). Public facts only, every claim sourced. Circle acts on a US or French authority or court; an Italian (or other non-US/FR) authority goes cross-border: an EU freezing order / EIO to France (Circle's EU entity is a French-licensed e-money institution), an MLAT to the US, or US counsel. No return by burn-and-reissue.
notes: Frozen is true only when the Blacklisted(address) event / isBlacklisted() of the native USDC or EURC contract says so (app/freeze). Bridged variants (e.g. USDC.e) are not controlled by Circle. Circle states it cannot burn and reissue USDC held in third-party wallets, so no funds_returned outcome is modelled; a general freeze-and-mint arrangement with US federal prosecutors for victims is reported (s6, medium), not documented by Circle.

entities.name: Circle EU entity (French-licensed e-money institution, EURC / USDC under MiCA)
entities.notes: Medium confidence: from Circle's MiCA white paper.

circle.blocklisting.notes: Freeze requests for addresses holding native USDC, as named by Circle's own compliance@ auto-reply. Circle acts on a US or French authority or court order: a private notice here flags the addresses and draws the 'court order required' answer.

circle.subpoenas.notes: Subpoenas and legal process for Circle records (named by the same auto-reply).

instrument.notes: A police / IC3 reference strengthens the notice; it is not an instrument.

paths.notes: Expect a refusal or 'court order required': Circle acts only when legally compelled through lawful process. The value is the early flag while the funds sit, and the exact instrument and channel it names.

instrument.notes: Policy exception: an urgent request by a US or French authority pending a court order of competent jurisdiction.

paths.notes: Policy Part 3, exception 3: Circle 'may block individual addresses in response to (i) certain urgent law enforcement requests pending a valid court order from a court of competent jurisdiction'. The exception names no country: the US/FR limit is inferred from the policy's US or French courts. Prosecutors report Circle denied freeze requests made without a court order (s5): treat as discretionary and rarely granted.

instrument.notes: An order of a US court of competent jurisdiction (the policy names Delaware or Massachusetts) or a French court; private counsel can obtain one (US TRO / attachment). Circle 'reserves all rights to object' to an order it finds objectionable. Policy Part 3 (exception 2) also accepts another governmental authority with jurisdiction over Circle. Aegis advice: name each address precisely (over-broad orders have caused wrongful freezes).

paths.notes: Fast once a valid order is served (same day in reported cases). Orders of other US state courts have been complied with in reported cases (a Wisconsin county court freeze, Aug 2025, s6: reported, medium) but Circle may object to them: prefer a Delaware or Massachusetts court, or a federal one there. A later burn-and-reissue warrant was refused. Over-broad orders have caused wrongful freezes: name addresses precisely.

instrument.notes: An EU judicial authority (e.g. an Italian PM / GIP) issues a Reg. (EU) 2018/1805 freezing certificate to France, where Circle's EU entity is licensed; the French authority's order is then one Circle acts on.

deadlines.action: Only when the certificate states that immediate freezing is necessary (Reg. 2018/1805 Art. 9(3)): the French executing authority decides on recognition within 48 hours of receipt. Otherwise there is no fixed limit, only 'without delay' (Art. 9(1)): for live funds the issuing PM ticks immediate freezing.

The executing authority takes the concrete freezing measures within 48 hours of the recognition decision (Art. 9(4)), whether or not immediate freezing was certified; only the 48-hour recognition limit depends on that (Art. 9(3)).

paths.notes: Inferred route: the policy names French authorities; the EU entity's French licence is medium confidence. Not for civil proceedings.

instrument.notes: European Investigation Order to France for Circle EU records.
A foreign court order pending completion of the MLAT process is a policy exception (medium confidence).

paths.notes: Policy Part 3, exception 3 (iii): Circle may block addresses on 'certain court orders pending completion of the Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty process'. MLAT averaged about 10 months in 2013-14 data (old): too slow alone for live funds; pair it with US counsel or an EU freezing order.
Inferred: only Circle account (Circle Mint) customers are onboarded with KYC under the USDC terms; self-custody holders have none.

instrument.notes: Formal confirmation from the authority or court that ordered the block that it is lifted.

paths.notes: Lifting shows as UnBlacklisted on-chain. Restitution goes through the court proceedings, not a reissue.
